'''Sumiyoshi Shrine''' (住吉神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Kato City]], [[Hyōgo Prefecture]]. The enshrined deities are the [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|Sumiyoshi Sanjin]] (Kamutsutsuno-o no Mikoto, Nakatsutsuno-o no Mikoto, Sokotsutsuno-o no Mikoto) and [[Empress Jingū|Okinaga Tarashihime no Mikoto]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha (small shrine)|ja|式内小社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha (small shrine)|qq=}} under the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]], and its former shrine Rank under the {{ill|Modern shrine Rank system|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern shrine Rank system|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}} was that of a village shrine. It is also referred to as the '''Kamikamogawa Sumiyoshi Shrine''' due to its location.
== Overview ==
The founding of the shrine is unknown.
The shrine precinct features a main hall, a divided worship hall (割拝殿), a long hall (長床), and a dance stage (舞殿), arranged around a central courtyard, preserving an ancient shrine layout.
It served as the tutelary shrine of Kamikamogawa Village. The main hall is designated as an [[Important Cultural Property]] of Japan and is recorded to have been constructed in the mid-[[Muromachi period]] during the second year of {{ill|Meiō|ja|明応|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiō|qq=}} (1493).
== Cultural Properties ==
[[File:Kamikamogawa Sumiyoshi Jinja 07.JPG|thumb|Main hall (National Important Cultural Property)]]
=== Important Cultural Property (Nationally Designated) ===
* Main Hall  
*: The main hall, constructed in the {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagare-zukuri|qq=}} style with a cypress bark roof, was first built in the late {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamakura period|qq=}} in the fifth year of {{ill|Shōwa|ja|正和|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa|qq=}} (1316). It was rebuilt during the mid-Muromachi period in the sixth year of {{ill|Eikyō|ja|永享|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyō|qq=}} (1434), and again in 1493 during Meiō 2. Records of its construction are preserved in inscriptions on ridge beams. The porch underwent repairs in the third year of {{ill|Jōkyō|ja|貞享|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōkyō|qq=}} (1686). It features a unique regional style, with the inner sanctuary raised on a higher platform. Reused old materials under the floor suggest the structure was originally a four-bay building. Designated on June 9, 1960.
=== Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property (Nationally Designated) ===
* Kamikamogawa Sumiyoshi Shrine Shinji Dance  
*: Designated on May 17, 1977. For details, see ''[[Kamikamogawa Sumiyoshi Shrine Shinji Dance]]''.
=== Hyōgo Prefectural Cultural Property ===
* Shinji Noh Masks  
*: Twelve noh masks used for the sacred dance survive. Of these, five masks—black old man, young man, father, old man, and king—are still used in ceremonies today. The remaining seven masks (old man, young man, old woman, prince, etc.) have unclear uses. Designated on March 29, 1968.
